generatedProse.concept-context: In a sport or exercise study, research integrity is one thread from your proposal to your write-up. The ethical care you promise your athletes or participants shapes how you handle their performance and health data, which shapes what you can honestly report about your results. When that thread holds, coaches and examiners can trust your findings and you can defend your method.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport-science students test the same training intervention. One clears ethics early, keeps athletes' health data loosely on a phone, and reports gains the approved protocol never measured. The other sets ethical principles up front, protects each athlete's data as promised, and keeps the method, approval and final analysis aligned. When a supervisor questions the results, only the second student can defend every decision.
generatedProse.summary: In your sport study, integrity is strongest when ethics, data handling and rigour work as one. You carry a single commitment from proposal to write-up, so each finding can be trusted and defended. It is that one practice, not any single strand, that makes your research sound.

check.body: A researcher sets ethical principles in the proposal, protects participant data as promised, and keeps the method matching approval right through to the dissertation. What does this show?

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That research integrity is one practice: the same commitment held steady across every stage of the project.
_items.feedback: Yes. Ethics, data and rigour worked as one from start to finish.

_items.text: That the researcher wasted effort by repeating the same check three times.
_items.feedback: These are not repeats. Each strand protects a different part of the same integrity.

_items.text: That only the dissertation stage really matters for integrity.
_items.feedback: Integrity had to hold at every stage, not just the last one.

_items.text: That ethical approval alone guarantees a rigorous project.
_items.feedback: Approval is one step. Rigour is sustained by decisions across the whole project.
